post.hook: Nvidia's rough day, two new Claude models
post.subhook: Plus llama.cpp hits 1.0 and Runway opens a robot controller

stories.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
stories.detail: Two new Claude model versions are out for practitioners to evaluate against their current Claude setups.

stories.headline: Reports: banned Nvidia chips trained Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4
stories.detail: If the reports hold, they point to export-control gaps that could change how China's leading open models are assessed and regulated.

stories.headline: llama.cpp reaches version 1.0
stories.detail: The local inference library marks a stability milestone and ships with an API version boundary note for developers building on it.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO
stories.detail: He leaves amid a scandal and investigations; a leadership change at the top AI chip supplier could affect chip supply and policy.

stories.headline: Runway opens Praxis-1 robot controller under Apache 2.0
stories.detail: Open weights and code for a video-trained controller, though it cannot yet plan complex action sequences on its own.

stories.headline: WSJ: Nvidia chips reached China via Southeast Asian data centers
stories.detail: The report describes a sanctions gap that may have let Chinese companies access restricted Nvidia AI chips.

stories.headline: llama.cpp b12406 adds Inkling 2 text and vision
stories.detail: Local llama.cpp users can run Inkling 2 text and vision models with this release, per the release notes.

stories.headline: OpenAI dissolves standalone robotics team
stories.detail: OpenAI says general-purpose models such as GPT-6 Astra can control robots directly, so its robotics researchers move to other teams.

stories.headline: Amodei addresses compute costs days before Anthropic IPO
stories.detail: Reported commitments of nearly $901 billion raise questions about whether future revenue will cover compute spending.

post.caption:
Two new Claude models and a very bad day for Nvidia lead today's AI news.

1. Anthropic introduces Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, ready to test against your current Claude setup. (SD Times)
2. Reports say export-banned Nvidia chips were used to train Kimi K3 and DeepSeek V4, pointing to gaps in export controls. (TechCrunch)
3. llama.cpp reaches 1.0, a stability milestone with an API version boundary note. (tbreak)
4. Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO amid a scandal and investigations. (The Guardian)
5. Runway releases Praxis-1, an open-weight, video-trained robot controller under Apache 2.0. It can't yet plan complex action sequences alone. (The Decoder)
6. WSJ reports Nvidia chips reached Chinese firms through Southeast Asian data centers via a sanctions gap. (Techmeme)
7. llama.cpp b12406 adds Inkling 2 text and vision support. (llama.cpp on GitHub)
8. OpenAI reassigns its robotics researchers, saying general models like GPT-6 Astra can control robots directly. (The Decoder)
9. Amodei addresses compute costs days before Anthropic's planned IPO, with reported commitments of nearly $901 billion. (The Decoder)

Export controls had a worse day than any model did. 🔍
